summary: Evening 5xx spike for NimbusHealth: HTTP/2 SETTINGS + aggressive keepalive producing streaming resets and upstream runtime crashes
description:
Issue summary:
Evening of 2026-03-13 we observed a sustained uptick in 5xx responses for requests originating from NimbusHealth (dedicated tenant) targeting streaming chat endpoints. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.2% to ~7% across a 40 minute window.

Impact:
- Customer observed failed streaming sessions and truncated responses for interactive chat flows (clinical triage UI).
- Estimated ~12% of active sessions for NimbusHealth experienced at least one 5xx.
- No data loss reported, but UX degraded (timeouts and reconnects).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dpool-us-east-9 (gpu-config: a100-80GB)
- API gateway cluster: apigw-us-east-02 (HTTP/2 enabled)
- Proxy: streaming-proxy-v2 (env=prod)
- Models: rw-v1-chat-8k pinned v2026-03-01

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer establishes long-lived streaming sessions with aggressive client keepalive: client interval 1s, timeout 3s.
2) High concurrency warmup (tenant concurrency climbed from 120 -> 420 over 6 minutes).
3) API gateway begins returning 503/502 for some streaming sessions; upstream serving-runtime logs show connection resets and watcher restarts.

Observed behavior / logs snippet:
- apigw metrics: http2.reset_count spiked +320 in 6m; accept_queue dropped to 40% capacity.
- streaming-proxy logs: repeated "RST_STREAM: PROTOCOL_ERROR (HTTP2_SETTINGS_TIMEOUT)" and "peer closed stream: ENHANCED_CONNECTIVITY_RESET".
- serving-runtime: N lines indicating "watchdog: runtime restart due to OOM (gpu mem fragmented)" and several core dumps during watchdog resets.

Expected behavior:
- Keepalive negotiation should not cause protocol resets. Our proxies and gateways should handle aggressive keepalive from clients without amplifying to upstream restarts.

Initial hypothesis:
1) Aggressive per-connection keepalive combined with HTTP/2 SETTINGS timing differences between apigw and streaming-proxy caused repeated settings re-negotiation and RST_STREAMs.
2) RSTs produced cascaded aborts that left GPU KV cache state inconsistent, leading to increased memory fragmentation and occasional serving-runtime OOMs.
3) Autoscaler / HPA warmup created a short-lived surge in ephemeral workers that amplified accept-queue pressure and threadpool oversubscription on the proxy.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support instructed customer to increase client keepalive interval to 10s (immediate reduction in resets reported).
- Deployed short-lived throttle patch at apigw to cap per-tenant concurrent handshake rate (rollout to apigw-us-east-02 completed 2026-03-13 22:14 UTC).
- SRE triggered a rolling restart of streaming-proxy-v2 instances to clear fragmented socket state (completed by 22:28 UTC).

Current status and impact assessment:
- Error rate reduced to ~0.6% after mitigations; still above baseline.
- Serving-runtime crashes have stopped after proxy restarts but KV cache evictions increased; monitoring collection ongoing.

Next steps / Proposed fixes:
- Engineering to add defensive backoff for HTTP/2 SETTINGS ack/timeouts in streaming-proxy to avoid RST storms (ENG-PR queued).
- Add per-connection keepalive advisory and enforceable soft limits for dedicated tenants in apigw config.
- Follow-up: run memory fragmentation and KV cache durability loadtest with aggressive connection churn to validate fixes.

References:
- Slack: #support-nimbushealth thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C045NIMBUS/p1678901234567
- Metrics dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/apigw/streaming-health?orgId=1&var-tenant=nimbushealth
comments: 2026-03-13 21:58 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer reported spike in streaming failures. Initial triage shows apigw returning 503 and multiple RST_STREAMs. Escalating to SRE.

2026-03-13 22:05 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Observed http2.reset_count spike and proxy threadpool saturation. Hypothesis: SETTINGS/keepalive mismatch. Requesting customer to temporarily increase keepalive to 10s. Applying limited ingress handshake rate cap as hotfix.
2026-03-13 22:20 - Customer (N. Patel, NimbusHealth): Confirmed reduced failures after increasing keepalive. UX still degraded for some sessions. Please advise next steps to avoid recurrence.

2026-03-13 22:32 - Eng (Priya Shah): Created GH PR to add backoff and settings-ack tolerance in streaming-proxy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/4123. Will bench test in staging and then coordinate canary release.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Follow-up with customer scheduled 2026-03-14 15:00 local. Add advisory to dedicated onboarding docs regarding keepalive recommendations.

2026-03-14 14:50 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Runbook note: add check for http2.SETTINGS negotiation failures to auto-trigger proxy restart and temporarily cap handshakes per-tenant. Filed INT-42010 for runbook update.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between tenant concurrency ramp and resets. Heap/kv metrics show fragmentation spike concurrent with reset window. No evidence of model binary issues. Priority is reducing protocol-level noise and ensuring proxy tolerates aggressive clients.
resolution_notes: Short-term: customer increased keepalive and apigw handshake cap deployed; proxy restarted to clear fragmented socket state. Medium-term: patch streaming-proxy to tolerate settings negotiation variance; update dedicated tenant advisory; add healthcheck to detect SETTINGS storm.

resolution: Partial mitigation applied; monitoring continues. Pending engineering fix and formal runbook updates.
